subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw define a public memory-plugin dreaming provider protocol in core, or keep dreaming orchestration owned by individual plugins and ClawHub packages?
rationale: The request adds public plugin-SDK, config, scheduler, and persisted-memory behavior surface; current main only has selected-slot config plus a memory-core sidecar, and the open role-slot PR does not settle the full Light/REM/Deep provider contract.

options.title: Coordinate a core provider contract
options.body: Use this issue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 or a follow-up design PR to define the API, role-slot semantics, migration behavior, docs, and proof for alternate memory plugins.

options.title: Keep dreaming plugin-owned
options.body: Document that LanceDB/vector-native dreaming should remain in ClawHub packages such as memory-lancedb-dreaming unless a missing core seam is identified.

options.title: Stage only docs now
options.body: Land generic docs about selected-slot dreaming settings and ClawHub discovery while leaving the public provider protocol undecided.

recommendation.title: Coordinate a core provider contract
recommendation.body: Use this issue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 or a follow-up design PR to define the API, role-slot semantics, migration behavior, docs, and proof for alternate memory plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a public OpenClaw product/API direction, and steipete is the listed project decision owner in CONTRIBUTING.md.
